<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Execute Resource Command"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/actions/{command}"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



The request body allows only a non-empty `id` and an optional `input` object. Unknown fields are rejected. Available commands and configuration follow the current resource type definition and the instance `commands`.
`create` acts directly on the parent resource: a protocol catalog creates only a Network, a Network creates a Device, and a Device creates a Point. `input` accepts only the required `config` and an optional `name`. Pass the display name only as the outer `name`; `config.name`/`config.friendlyName` are rejected. A successful response returns only `id`/`type`; read the details separately.
`discover` acts directly on a Network (discover devices) or a Device (discover points). Catalogs do not provide `discover`. `input` contains only optional `options` and may be omitted. `options` accepts only slash-path keys from `optionsSchema` with non-null scalar values. Read-only fields and the flow-control field `autoCreate` cannot be overridden; hidden writable fields may be overridden. Discovery does not automatically add resources.
`import` acts on a discovery Job. `input` must contain 1–200 `discoveryObjectIds` and exactly one of `networkId` (import devices) or `deviceId` (import points; Open device ID). `ownerId` and `pointConfigs` are not accepted. The server validates job ownership, target type, protocol, and permissions for the whole batch, then checks `results` item by item. Successful items contain only `resource.id`/`type`; failed items contain `errorCode`/`message`.
`delete` acts on an actual instance, with `input` as an empty object. Deletion permissions and status are checked again at execution time.
Device connection diagnostics use `deviceId` and remain compatible with `targetId`. Point diagnostics still use the Point `targetId`.

For a `sequence` resource `create`, `id` is `sequence`. `input` allows `name`, `data`, `icon`, and `deviceId`, of which `name`, `data`, and `deviceId` are required.
`deviceId` identifies the device that the scene is created for. `create` accepts only `data.type=commands` and does not accept `unavailable`.
